G01.screen: MakeUp native100 maintained copy/scalar route is executable. Complementary has an existing exact-source composite3 identity-pass prototype (texelFetch colortex0 -> same R11F_G11F_B10F), but no maintained physical-lifetime comparison yet. BSL has no maintained equivalent copy-elision route. Existing history rotation/exchange implementations require substantial additional ownership and full-clear proofs and remain MakeUp-specific.
G01.bound: Use actual retained-copy bytes and parsed identity-pass dimensions as an optimistic bandwidth-work bound; copies submitted are not GPU time or proven dead history.

G02.screen: Maintained public routes exist for BSL and both Complementary profiles, with actual mip/source observer. Inspect MakeUp native mip inventory before claiming an opportunity. Public adapter overhead must be distinguished from the underlying omission; existing native-only BSL discriminator is an independent alternative.

G03.screen: All four have existing consumers. Added BSL/Complementary read-only family permission counters to the maintained harness; source readiness and qualified progress required. MakeUp has a separately witnessed Asahi post-sample rewrite. Admission counts do not count avoided fragments.

G04.mechanism: Skip noncontributing translucent lighting / cloud work
G04.screen: The maintained implementation is MakeUp-native shader math, with a restored honey fixture for non-water/glass coverage. Other targets lack an equivalent maintained transform. A MakeUp gain alone cannot support a shared v1 implementation. Overlap with G03/N04 work avoidance must not be double-counted.

G05.screen: Use existing next-event/identical-coordinate consumers across all four. Do not infer actual sampler permission or saved queries from request flags. Historical MakeUp fixed16 hierarchy lost; the cheaper existing reuse route is a distinct alternative, not that negative result.

G06.screen: MakeUp exact attenuation guard and other targets half-resolution AO are different implementations of the goal; identify that explicitly. Half AO can refuse without a current producer/target proof and needs separate visual acceptance. MakeUp G06 and N04 sky/attenuation guards overlap; no additive claim.

G07.screen: Existing AO depth reuse consumers on all four retain native implicit sampling unless the current sampler proof permits reuse. Default/unqualified is a fallback case. Temporal filtering is a distinct, separately input/proof-constrained route.

G08.screen: MakeUp native cloud bound is a maintained private route. Complementary GetSky/local lighting reuse exists. BSL has no operative volume_light_reuse consumer; its separate primary-cloud density bound is clear-weather Balanced-only with explicit-LOD sampler qualification and an old target-specific integration. Do not remove its profile/sampler guards or describe it as tested by a Performance lighting-reuse flag.

G09.screen: MakeUp native has no POM traversal. BSL full-PBR Replete profile is separately measured with private functional proof; synthetic ray/query omissions do not count actual rendered skip hits. Complementary native RP_MODE1 is a useful no-POM fallback case; it cannot establish PBR benefit.

G10.screen: Maintained exact MakeUp bloom route has pre-detach link/draw and integer opportunity witnesses. Historical opportunity bound was at most 0.00427% of source-query expressions in that tuple. No maintained equivalents on other targets; approximate pairing lacks native precision guarantees. Stop a weak bound before three pack-specific ports.

C01.screen: Maintained private bounds-query route pins MakeUp native opaque geometry. Test natural-cave opportunity using the existing GPU deferred mode; keep source and actual query/read requirements. Other targets need a shared geometry/occluder proof. Depth priming is a different route and is not silently substituted for the bounds-query candidate.

C02.screen: Required NV extensions absent on Asahi; all four cells are hardware-unsupported, never zero speedup. The current backend is vendor-specific and outside shared-vendor v1 implementation scope. No hardware restriction is removed.

N01.mechanism: CPU command compaction / admission and scalar caching
N01.screen: Shared renderer path, tested as its dependency bundle on all four in the prepared natural world. Actual consuming batches/hits and stable native pipeline identities required. Command entries are not GL draws; total-frame speed and scoped render CPU cost remain distinct.

N02.mechanism: Eliminate unused attachments and target pairs
N02.screen: Existing source/physical prototypes are Bliss/Photon, outside initial targets. Inventory each native target graph and current/next-frame readers, image/compute roots and writes before any deletion. Parsed availability and absent sampler names alone are not lifetime proof. Do not port a pack-specific dead output solely to fill the table.

N03.mechanism: Eliminate terminal copies with dead lifetime

Actual final-copy inventory is gathered on all four via N01; deleting histories or changing bank rotation requires complete ordering/clear/reader proof. No independent credit for the same omitted copies.
